questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

I don't mind trying to make your day as well as you make mine.

options.text: as well as you make mine

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the** incorrect comparison** between "make your day" and "make mine."
 
• The phrase should be corrected to "I don't mind trying to make your day **as you make mine**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I don't mind trying to make your day** as you make mine**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1) "I don't mind trying,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **2) "to make your day,"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **3) "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 4.

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Some of the flowers in my garden is not blooming properly.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the subject-verb agreement.
 
• "Some of the flowers" is a plural subject and should be followed by a plural verb.
 
• The correct verb form should be** "are"** instead of** "is".**
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Some of the flowers in my garden **are not blooming properly.**"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "flowers in my garden," **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **2: "No error" **– This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error.
 
• **3: "Some of the," **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **4: "is not blooming properly." **– This part of the sentence has a **grammatical error** as explained.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

He said he would split open a raw Irish potato and stick the quarter in _________ and keep it there all night.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is identifying the correct preposition that fits the context.
 
• The phrase **"split open a raw Irish potato and stick the quarter in"** suggests placing the potato quarter in a confined space.
 
• The preposition** "between" **correctly conveys the idea of placing the quarter in a space confined by two other objects or parts.
 
• Thus, the preposition **"between"** is the most appropriate choice for the blank.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said he would split open a raw Irish potato and stick the quarter in **between** and keep it there all night."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: slice** – This does not fit the context as it implies a thin piece of something, which does not make sense here.
 
• **Option 3: gap** – This is close but less specific compared to "between" and does not convey the same confined space.
 
• **Option 4: along** – This preposition does not fit the context as it implies movement in a line, which is not intended here.

The main driver of today's global warming were the combustion of fossil fuels.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect verb usage.** "Were"** should be replaced with** "was" **to match the singular noun **"driver."**
 
• In this sentence,** "The main driver" **is a singular subject, which requires a singular verb **"was," not "were."**
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase should be **"The main driver of today's global warming was the combustion of fossil fuels," **ensuring subject-verb agreement.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The main driver of today's global warming** was **the combustion of fossil fuels."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 3: "The main driver of"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "combustion of fossil fuels"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
